title: Per-tenant admission gating and region-aware failover for Dedicated/Private
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: During region-level incidents and rolling upgrades we observe correlated tenant failures that cause noisy neighbor effects and cascading control-plane pressure. Existing tenant isolation mechanisms are coarse (tenant quarantine / evictions) and lack admission gates that are both tenant- and region-aware. We need a predictable, testable admission control layer that enforces per-tenant SLO budgets, supports staged degrade modes, and integrates with multi-region failover and rolling upgrade safety checks for Dedicated and Private deployments.

This ticket implements a per-tenant admission gating system ("circuit gating") plus a region-aware failover policy and upgrade preflight checks. The goal is to contain incident blast radius, keep high-priority tenants online, and provide clear observability and manual controls for operators.
design_decisions: Admission gate model: token-bucket admission per-tenant per-route with configurable thresholds (priority tiers: gold/silver/bronze).
Circuit states: CLOSED (normal), THROTTLE (soft degrade, increased latency), OPEN (reject), ISOLATE (route to local fallback/model or deny if none).
Region affinity: requests carry tenant-region affinity. When region health degrades, gate switches to REGION_DEGRADE which prefers local tolerant variants or triggers failover policy.

Failover policy: two-stage automated failover: 1) soft redirect to warm standby model variant in same cloud region; 2) if capacity insufficient, redirect to remote region per tenant priority and data locality rules.
Upgrade preflight: control-plane upgrade sequence must run tenant admission simulation (dry-run) using recent traffic traces; failures produce automated rollback or hold for manual approval.
Backpressure integration: tie admission gates to serving-runtime queue depth and KV-cache hit metrics to make admission decisions informed by runtime state.
Observability: expose per-tenant gate metrics (state, rejects, throttled tokens consumed) and SLO burn rates to Console and alerts.
Operator controls: console toggles for per-tenant emergency isolation, manual failover, and staged throttles.
tasks: Spec: write detailed design doc and configuration schema (done, link in comments)
Runtime: implement per-tenant token-bucket admission hooks in serving runtime (C++/Rust) with async path check
Control plane: add API to push per-tenant gate config and to query gate state
Failover: implement region-aware routing rules in ingress router and add warm-standby model registration
Upgrade hooks: implement preflight dry-run using replayed traces and gating simulator
Console: add UI for per-tenant gate view and manual controls
Observability: add metrics (prometheus) and tracing spans, wire to Console dashboards and alert rules
E2E tests: chaos tests that simulate region outage, capacity pressure, and rolling upgrades
Runbook: author incident playbook for gate state transitions and manual overrides
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant admission gates enforce token-bucket limits and transition through CLOSED/THROTTLE/OPEN/ISOLATE states under load
Region-aware failover routes traffic according to configured tenant priority and respects data-locality labels
Upgrade preflight detects unsafe upgrade plans in >90% of simulated overload scenarios and blocks rollout without manual approval
Metrics are emitted for gate state, rejects, throttled counts, and SLO burn-rate and visible in Console dashboard
Chaos test: when region A simulates 60% capacity loss, gold tenants maintain >= 99.5% success rate by failing over to standby
Operators can manually override gate state and trigger per-tenant failover from Console
Documentation: design doc, runbook, and migration plan published and linked
open_questions: What should be the default tenant priority mapping for self-serve Dedicated customers?
Should admission tokens be consumed per-token or per-request for streaming endpoints?
How to express strict data-locality constraints for Private on-prem tenants during failover?
What are safe default thresholds for THROTTLE and OPEN states for 1ms median-latency targets?
Do we need per-model vs per-route gating granularity initially or can routes be used as proxy?
risks: Incorrect thresholds could cause unnecessary rejections impacting revenue-sensitive tenants
Failover to remote regions may violate regulatory constraints for some Private customers
Admission gating adds additional latency to the request path if poorly optimized
Upgrade preflight false negatives could block safe rollouts if trace sampling is biased

notes: Migration approach: introduce gates as opt-in per-customer config for first rollout, default to permissive CLOSED state. After 2-week observation, flip to adaptive mode for tenants agreeing to SLA changes.
Performance target: admission check added to hot path must not add >1.0ms p50 to text/generation requests at 512 tokens on p4d-like hardware.
Telemetry sample: collect full request traces for 0.1% of traffic to validate gate simulator accuracy during preflight
Operators: add RBAC flag so only SRE and Customer Support can toggle emergency isolation for Private deployments
